title: Two validate fixtures escape the gate's cgroup into a sibling scope, so the official gate returns a null status
description:
- **Files:** `agent-utils/rs/dagrun/src/cgroup.rs` (:935 attempt_scope_reexec, :1758 Cgroups::new), `scripts/validate.rs` (:1343 submodule_failure_service_result_bracket, :1247 nested_scope_self_test, :19932, :4829), `scripts/lib/safe_ci_scope.rs` resolve_cgroups.
- **Action:** Give both fixtures an explicitly owned nested resource/cancellation root below the authenticated enclosing gate step, instead of a sibling scope. The report says the current API has NO explicit borrowed-root allocation parameter, so review the required API and fixture scope BEFORE implementing.
- **Why:** Both fixtures set DAGRUN_FORCE_SCOPE_ATTEMPT=1 and clear the scope sentinels, so resolve_cgroups starts a FRESH systemd scope under dagrun.slice — a SIBLING of the enclosing official scope. The gate's 5-GiB/one-CPU controls and its cancellation do not cover a sibling. Witnessed, not inferred: PID 170445, start_ticks 148533125, recorded in both the gate leaf under step-gate.manifest AND in dagrun-170445.scope, both memberships preserved for the same process identity before rescue. Consequence: the official gate attempt on https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/2694 self-interrupted at 417.3s and returned a NULL status — driver status and gate status both null. This is a gate that cannot produce a verdict, not a gate reporting a failure.
- **Second-order constraint (do not skip):** merely retaining the DAGRUN variables is NOT sufficient. `Cgroups::new` at cgroup.rs:1758 DRAINS EVERY PROCESS from its current leaf into supervisor before enabling controllers, so a nested caller in the shared gate leaf would move the gate runner and other fixture processes. The controller requires exact-leaf membership. A fix without explicit owned-subtree accounting trades one ownership gap for another.
- **Both fixtures, not one:** nested_scope_self_test at :1247 does the same thing and the full self-test invokes it at :2722 after the first missing-rr bracket. Fixing only the first bracket leaves a later escape. Its 30s scope / 45s wrapper bounds, inner success, and exact SIGTERM/surviving-sibling assertions must all remain, and its fresh RuntimeMax request must not be treated as satisfied by the enclosing scope's much longer runtime.
- **Rejected shortcuts, named in the report:** weakening the sampler; accepting short-lived siblings; copying per-child caps without aggregate/cancellation ownership; --allow-cgroup-failure; dropping either fixture or its second invocation; moving an unchecked shell precheck ahead of the DAG and claiming its executed-node count; relabelling the null status or the rescue -9 as a gate result. A starts-with exception, or ignoring a moving PID, is not a repair.
- **Verify:** Run the official gate on PR 2694 and read the terminal record. Acceptance is the set of controls the report names, each checked from the run's own artifacts: fixture child membership and enclosing effective caps observed BEFORE its real first-node execution; the original bootstrap and missing-rr status1/nodecount1 assertions still present and passing; a sibling-migration mutation REFUSED; parent and surviving sibling alive after nested SIGTERM; timeout cleanup empties the owned nested subtree without killing the enclosing scheduler; and an invalid or missing enclosing context refuses BEFORE any fixture process is released. A standalone native test must receive a genuinely observed enclosing context rather than fabricating environment sentinels.
- **Evidence:** /tmp/astra-reverie-2694-recovery/fixture-main-gate-interruption-diagnosis/report.md; manifest SHA256 61e364172bc44a4257bc67bba1bc0aa6eabd1b819abe86f9c113c1c0f34dd9bb binding 292 files / 1,001,028,471 bytes. That directory's generic FAILED heading means failed qualification only — the authoritative status fields are null. terminal-check.json and before_rescue-pid170445.json bind the two observations. The exact sibling's limits were NOT captured and must remain unknown.
- **Provenance:** diagnosed by agent(dev-hermit), read in full by the coordinator. No goalpost was moved: no assertion, threshold, selector, resource limit or comparator changed.

title: One malformed marker-shaped line makes changes-requested-gate return INDETERMINATE at every head
description:
- **Action:** Establish how many pull requests currently have a blinded gate for this reason, and make the failure degrade rather than blind. The tick reports 3 malformed source lines across 3 pull requests, so there are likely two more beyond https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/2694.
- **Why:** A gate that returns INDETERMINATE reads as 'cannot tell' and is treated as 'nothing to see'. On 2694 it hid six real objections and made a blocked pull request look merely unattended for twenty days — including to me, when I dispatched its review describing it as never reviewed with nothing known.
- **Verify:** Every pull request with a malformed marker named, with its gate state before and after repair. Then the mechanism fixed or the fix proposed with its tradeoff stated.
- **Mechanism already established, do not re-derive:** unresolved_review_objections raises ReviewRecordError if ANY malformed marker exists, BEFORE returning any objection. Driving the library with the one offending line fenced returned six objections that were otherwise invisible. Gate went rc=2 INDETERMINATE to rc=1 BLOCKED after repair.
- **This is the abort-before-verdict class this project has paid for twice already:** two August-17 ledger rows lacking later fields made every subsequent landing-facing status query exit before returning a verdict, and a receipt validator rejecting four fields the verifier legitimately emits meant no receipt could qualify for days. Same shape, third location.
- **The design question worth stating rather than assuming:** should one malformed line make the whole answer unavailable, or should the gate report the objections it CAN parse and name the lines it cannot? Fail-closed is right when the unparsed content might be an objection; it is wrong when it hides six objections that parsed fine. State the tradeoff rather than picking silently.
- **Vocabulary:** do not coin new terms in reporting or in anything written for a human; naming code identifiers is ordinary work.
